clue.text: Decline visit joining planter?

parts.note: to visit a place is to go to it
a planter is a container for plants, a pot

explanation.surface: A gardener declines an invitation to come and join someone at the planter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planter?' is a playful definition of a plant pot, the question mark flagging the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: things that go downhill through neglect are said to have gone this way, so it means deteriorate.

clue.text: Start to dismount

definitions.meaning: to begin, as in a race getting away to a good beginning
to climb down from a horse or bicycle

explanation.surface: Instructions for beginning to climb down from a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb with two senses: setting off at the start of something, and stepping down from a mount or vehicle.

clue.text: Short jerky motion of tense sorceress

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a sorceress is a witch

explanation.surface: A nervous sorceress makes a sudden little spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brief involuntary jerk of a muscle is exactly this kind of quick spasm.

clue.text: Mature artist put under pressure to produce an exciting book

indicators.note: in a down clue, the words placed under another piece come after it, so the pressure letter goes on top

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
to mature is to age
J. M. W. Turner, the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: An elderly painter, pressed hard, manages to write a gripping novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put under' means the age-and-artist pieces sit below P in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal term for a gripping book that makes the reader keep flipping onward to see what happens.

clue.text: First of items nicked by the female pickpocket?

indicators.note: something nicked by is held, stolen, by the surrounding letters, so the pick goes inside
the opening letter of the word items is taken

explanation.surface: A woman pickpocket snatches the first of several items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked by' puts I inside THE F; 'nicked' also means stolen, tying in with the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pickpocket is one kind of robber who steals, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Covered entrance to building of international company by harbour

parts.note: a harbour is a port

explanation.surface: A global firm's office near the docks has a sheltered doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the harbour beside the I and CO pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture: a porch of columns supporting a roof over the doorway of a building.

clue.text: Royal initially touched on American university

parts.note: a prince is a royal

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word touched is used

explanation.surface: A royal briefly mentions a US college in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Ivy League university in New Jersey.

clue.text: Authentic-sounding Highland dance?

indicators.note: -sounding says the word for authentic is to be heard, giving a word spoken alike

parts.note: authentic means real

explanation.surface: Asking whether a dance is a genuine Scottish one.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks that the dance is merely an example of the type.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lively Scottish folk dance, a staple of a ceilidh.

clue.text: Idle at home, one taking in ITV broadcast

parts.note: someone at home is in

indicators.note: taking in means holding within, so the reshuffled letters go inside

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of ITV are mixed up

explanation.surface: Lazing at home, someone takes in an ITV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV is a British commercial television channel; 'broadcast' scrambles its name rather than airing it, and 'taking in' sets the result inside the card.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something idle is not working or doing anything.

clue.text: Choose one film for glass half-full type?

parts.note: to choose is to opt
I is the Roman numeral for one
a film is a thin layer, like a mist on a surface

explanation.surface: Selecting a single movie that would suit a cheerful person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests a movie but means a thin coating, here mist.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone who sees the glass as half full rather than half empty is hopeful by nature.

clue.text: Fine golf article

parts.note: fine as in a fine thread means thin
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfing item described as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' reads as praise but means slender.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an article is an object or item.

clue.text: I can go on and on about European travelling from place to place

parts.note: a can is a tin
to go on and on is to rant

explanation.surface: Someone admits they can keep ranting about Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link: E simply sits before RANT, as the surface's ranting about Europe suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an itinerant worker moves about from town to town.

clue.text: Opposite view of expert

parts.note: a facet is an aspect or view of something
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert's opinion that runs contrary.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people sitting opposite are directly confronting one another.

clue.text: Tube stop

definitions.meaning: a thin pipe, like the slender stalk of a flower or the narrow tube of a pipe
to staunch a flow, such as bleeding

explanation.surface: Alighting at a London Underground station.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a slender stalk or pipe part, and the verb meaning to halt a flow.

clue.text: Says yes to acquiring assembly room for a feast day

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so the room goes inside

parts.note: saying yes to something allows it
a hall is a room for gatherings

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to book a function room for a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for All Saints' Day, the Christian festival on 1 November.

clue.text: Enlisted man is in play

parts.note: a private is the lowest rank of soldier
to be in a place is to live there

explanation.surface: A soldier is cast in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' looks like acting in a play but means resides.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a 1930 comedy by Noël Coward.

clue.text: Card from servant enclosing note, 'in love at last'

indicators.note: enclosing means holding around, so the note letter goes inside

parts.note: a valet is a manservant

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word love is taken

explanation.surface: A servant's card carries a note confessing love at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a greetings card sent anonymously on 14 February.

clue.text: A cold potato dish, constant problem

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
rösti is a Swiss dish of fried grated potato
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A chilly potato dish has become a never-ending headache.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a word puzzle where initial letters spell a word is a kind of brain-teaser.

clue.text: Male coming in to make a light meal

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the male letter goes inside

parts.note: to make is to create

explanation.surface: A man arrives to prepare a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside CREATE, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an English afternoon snack of scones, jam and clotted cream with tea.

clue.text: A free hand got by revolutionary bishop, in association with a knight, earlier

indicators.note: earlier says those pieces come before the revolutionary
in means placed inside, so the bishop goes within the association

parts.note: a cartel is an association of businesses
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
N is the chess notation for knight
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel and a bishop, teamed with a knight, are given freedom to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got by' is a link; 'earlier' puts CARTEBLAN before CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed French phrase meaning complete freedom to act as one sees fit, literally a blank card.

clue.text: Constant, therefore all the same

parts.note: something constant is even, unvarying
so means therefore

explanation.surface: A chain of reasoning: steady, hence unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: nevertheless, notwithstanding what has been said.

clue.text: Left in charge, tippler's opening red wine

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the left letter goes within

parts.note: something in your charge is in your care

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word tippler's

explanation.surface: Someone left in charge opens a drinker's bottle of red.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: British name for a red Bordeaux.

clue.text: 'Be-Bopa-Lula', in part, a gem

indicators.note: only a portion of the song title is used, the letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A rock'n'roll song title is part of a precious find.
explanation.walkthrough: The song is really spelt 'Be-Bop-a-Lula'; the setter has moved the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an iridescent precious stone.

clue.text: New article probing school exam is fair

indicators.note: probing means poking inside, so these letters go within the exam

parts.note: O level was the British school exam taken at about 16 before GCSEs
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A new article examining a school exam claims it is fair.
explanation.walkthrough: O LEVEL was the old British school exam at 16.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: honest and straightforward, above board.

clue.text: Very warm, the Spanish inn

parts.note: very warm means hot
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A sweltering Spanish guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are places offering paying guests lodging.

clue.text: Somewhere to sit, to date unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to date means so far

explanation.surface: A seat that so far has not been completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long upholstered couch for several people.

clue.text: One who leaves a lasting impression on one?

definitions.text: One who leaves a lasting impression on one?

parts.words: One who leaves a lasting impression on one?
parts.note: the phrase usually means someone memorable, but here the impression is literally inked into the skin

explanation.surface: Praise for someone memorable.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lasting impression' is normally figurative; here it is a permanent mark made on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal reading: an artist who inks permanent designs into a client's skin.

clue.text: Proprietor's depressing experience missing daughter

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the daughter letter is removed

parts.note: a downer is something depressing

explanation.surface: A shop proprietor has a gloomy time without a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a proprietor is a person who possesses a business or property.

clue.text: Artist in African country beginning to explain travesty

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the artist goes within the country

parts.note: Chad is a country in central Africa
RA, a Royal Academician

indicators.note: the first letter of the word explain

explanation.surface: A painter in Africa begins to explain a miscarriage of justice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an absurd pretence or sham, such as a trial that is a farce.

clue.text: Fail to benefit from moving to Seoul

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone misses out by relocating to the Korean capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to miss an opportunity or not gain an advantage.
